title: Web & app server — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: Two things live here, and the distinctive one isn't the web server. The HTTP server is real and competent — a reactor-driven HTTP/1.1 server with Express-like routing, built-in HTTPS/mTLS, an auto-CRUD sqlite backend, and (ahead of Express and FastAPI) a built-in per-request SLA bracket with Prometheus `/metrics` + distributed tracing, plus a mounted auth router that is also an OIDC provider. But it's missing modern-API table stakes: middleware is registered-but-never-invoked, no JSON request-body parsing, no streaming, no WebSocket. The standout is the service-virtualization plane — WireMock-and-beyond stateful doubles under a governance gate no competitor has: `Deploy(:Production)` structurally refuses a fake dependency, even for a fully-entitled human.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. The web-server lanes measure against Express and FastAPI; the virtualization lanes against WireMock — where the governance gate has no peer.

lanes.engine: A per-request bracket around parse→route→handler→write recording well-known subjects `http.request.ms` / `http.requests` / `http.errors` and a labeled `http.route.ms` family, over engine histograms (p50/p95/p99). Built-in `/health` and Prometheus `/metrics`, plus W3C `traceparent` propagation.
lanes.owed: Observability is built in, not bolted on — ahead of Express/FastAPI, which need middleware libraries for the same. Per-route percentiles and tracing ship by default.

lanes.engine: `MountAuth` serves login / 2FA / logout / magic-link / OTP with HttpOnly + SameSite cookies and CSRF; `MountOidcProvider` makes the server an IdP (discovery, JWKS, authorize, PKCE token); off-loopback listeners take `RequireSignedRequests` (HMAC, clock-skew, nonce replay).
lanes.owed: An auth router and an OIDC provider built into the server — beyond what Express/FastAPI ship. Wired to the security plane's `stzAuth` / `stzRequestSigner`.

lanes.engine: Behavior-accurate sandboxes, not just canned responses: a payment state machine (authorize→capture-once, refund≤captured, integer minor units, assertable ledger), an LLM double with cost accounting, mail/SMS capture sinks (SMS counts billable segments), a local-real blob store, and real signing OIDC/passkey doubles.
lanes.owed: These enforce the rules of the real service (you cannot capture twice, refund more than you took) — well beyond WireMock's response stubbing. A genuinely distinctive testing surface.

lanes.engine: Every bound service carries a posture (sandbox / local / live); five registry invariants (`sandbox-in-production`, `live-without-secret`, `ephemeral-in-production`…) plus part-level graph rules. At the crossing, `stzDelivery.Deploy` refuses even a fully-entitled human if the surface is unsound, logs an incident, and returns a rehearsal.
lanes.owed: "Shipping a fake payment gateway is not an authority question." No peer has a structural gate that makes fakes-in-production unrepresentable — and the fail-open snapshot bug that once broke it is fixed and guarded.

lanes.engine: A real HTTP/1.1 server: the engine (`reactor.zig` + `http_framing.zig`) does async accept + framing on the libuv thread; Ring drains events and dispatches synchronously (`ServeOne` / `Run`), with keep-alive and `Connection: close` handling.
lanes.owed: HTTP/1.1 only server-side (HTTP/2 is client-only, via curl), and one request per `ServeOne` — no concurrent in-Ring handling. A genuine server, at a single-threaded dispatch tier.

lanes.engine: `stzAppRouter`: `Get_`/`Post`/`Put_`/`Delete`, path params (`:id`, multi-param), trailing `*` wildcard, exact-first then first-pattern-wins.
lanes.owed: Express-shaped and works, but no route groups, no regex constraints on params, and no method-not-allowed vs not-found distinction.

lanes.engine: `StartTls` / `StartHttps` with mbedTLS termination below the router, and mutual TLS (`bRequireClient` + CA path) — handlers run on decrypted bytes.
lanes.owed: HTTPS + mTLS built in, where Express/FastAPI usually delegate TLS to a reverse proxy. Test certs only — no managed cert lifecycle (shared with the concurrency plane's mTLS note).

lanes.engine: `Expose` / `ExposeWithKey` generate a full REST CRUD surface over sqlite — `/api/<table>` list / count / read / create / update / delete, SQL-escaped.
lanes.owed: A genuine auto-backend Express/FastAPI don't ship — but sqlite-only and basic: no relations, filtering, pagination or projection depth.

lanes.engine: `stzHttpSandbox`: `Script` (exact / prefix / contains matching), canned + JSON + failure responses, record/replay keyed by `sha256(method|url|body)` (a recording wins over a script), strict-by-default (unscripted requests raise), and a journal (`NumberOfCallsTo` catches retry storms).
lanes.owed: Matching is three patterns (no header / body / regex matchers WireMock has), there is no latency injection, and the live adapter reports only 200/0 (no status line from the curl client).

lanes.engine: `stzAppRequest` (Query / Header / Body / Param, case-insensitive headers, form-urlencoded parse) and `stzAppResponse` (Status / Header / Json / Text / Html / Send).
lanes.owed: No JSON request-body parsing (only serialize-out), no multipart, and no streaming responses (the body is always buffered with a fixed `Content-Length`). Real gaps for a modern JSON API.

lanes.engine: Static routes and hosted-agent surfaces are registered; `/health` and `/metrics` ship.
lanes.owed: Absent: WebSocket serving, OpenAPI/schema, content negotiation, server-side rate limiting, templating — and static file serving is registered but never served. The breadth FastAPI/Express are chosen for.

The middleware is registered but never invoked — `_Dispatch` has no execution path for `@aMiddleware`. Middleware is the Express model, so this is the biggest single missing mechanism: without it, cross-cutting concerns (CORS, logging, auth guards) can't compose.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first wires the mechanisms that already have a registration surface and the body handling a JSON API needs; the second fills the real-time and static edges; the third is the FastAPI-grade breadth.

items.title: Execute the middleware pipeline
items.text: `Use`/`AddMiddleware` already store handlers — `_Dispatch` just never runs them. Wiring the chain (before/after route) is the single highest-leverage fix: it turns CORS, logging, auth-guards and rate-limits from impossible into one-liners.

items.title: JSON request bodies + streaming responses
items.text: Parse an inbound JSON body into a value (today only form-urlencoded parses; JSON is serialize-out only), and stream a response instead of always buffering to a fixed `Content-Length`. Both are table stakes for a JSON/API server.

tiers.title: Tier B — real-time & the mocking edges

items.title: Serve static files
items.text: `Static`/`AddStaticRoute` are registered into `@aStaticRoutes` but nothing serves them. Finish the dead path — a small, expected capability.

items.title: WebSocket serving
items.text: Server-side WebSocket over the reactor — absent today. Needed for any real-time surface (live dashboards, agent streams, the GUI reactive layer over the wire).

items.title: Latency injection + a status-aware live adapter
items.text: The HTTP sandbox's two WireMock-parity gaps: a delay knob for latency/timeout simulation, and a live client that returns the real status line (today only 200/0). Small, and they complete the record/replay story.

items.title: OpenAPI, schema & content negotiation
items.text: Body-schema validation, a generated OpenAPI document, and Accept/Accept-Language handling — the FastAPI surface that turns routes into a documented, validated API.

items.title: HTTP/2 (server) & richer matching
items.text: Server-side HTTP/2 (the client already has it via curl+nghttp2), and header/body/regex request matchers in the sandbox toward full WireMock parity.

items.title: Deeper MBaaS
items.text: Relations, filtering, pagination and projection on the auto-CRUD backend, and a datasource beyond sqlite — the step from a demo backend to a deployable one.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main`. The reactor server, MBaaS CRUD and IoT listener are guarded by real end-to-end narrated tests (a second reactor as the client, sqlite persistence verified), and the service plane is heavily guarded (~370 assertions — registry, ports, delivery — living under `test/system`, since `test/service` is empty). Two things to note: three legacy appserver tests fail with a `C22` function-redefinition (structural, not behavioral — the narrated guards are what vouch for the server), and two capabilities (middleware, static) are registered but never executed — the advertised surface exceeds the wired one. A critical governance bug is fixed and recorded: the registry once snapshotted state and could fail open on a later fake-bind; it is now keyed by id so every copy is the registry.

Softanza's web tier is a competent-not-remarkable HTTP server whose real distinction is everything around the request — built-in SLA observability, a built-in auth provider, and a stateful service-virtualization plane gated so a fake can't reach production — while its distance from Express/FastAPI is the ergonomic middle (middleware, JSON bodies, streaming, WebSocket, OpenAPI) it has scoped but not fully wired.
